claims.claim: Rettberg's proposed mechanism is that LLMs generate text associatively, so a route or place token pulls in the promotional register that surrounds it in the training data.
The New York Times told Rettberg that the journalist who wrote her first example confirmed she did not use AI to write it.
claims.source: Jill Walker Rettberg, jilltxt.net, update of 14 May 2026
claims.quote: she did not use AI to write this

claims.claim: A public library services manager says today's AI-generated books are quite bad, to the point of asking whether an alien wrote this.
claims.source: Kate DeMeester-Lane, library services manager, Pima County Public Library, quoted by Jule Pattison-Gordon, Governing, 3 October 2025

claims.claim: The same librarian says the first pages of an AI-generated book quickly reveal it because the content doesn't make sense.
claims.source: Kate DeMeester-Lane quoted by Jule Pattison-Gordon, Governing, 3 October 2025

claims.claim: A Carnegie Mellon machine-learning professor says the model doesn't know the difference between travel advice, directions or recipes and just knows words.

claims.quote: It doesn't know the difference between travel advice, directions or recipes
claims.page: middle section on how AI generates answers

claims.claim: A 2024 survey reported by the BBC found around 33% of respondents who used AI to plan travel said their AI-generated recommendations included false information.
claims.source: a 2024 survey as reported by BBC Travel, 26 September 2025
claims.quote: 33% said their AI-generated recommendations included false information

claims.claim: The same 2024 survey found 37% of those who used AI to plan travel reported that it could not provide enough information.
claims.source: a 2024 survey as reported by BBC Travel, 26 September 2025
claims.quote: 37% of those surveyed who used AI to help plan their travels reported that it could not provide enough information

claims.claim: A measurement study of AI urban perception found that culturally proximate prompting fails to recover the variety and diversity of human responses.
claims.source: Rong Zhao and four co-authors, 'Culturally uneven urban perception in large language models', arXiv 2604.20048v3, 8 June 2026
claims.quote: fails to recover the variety and diversity of human responses

claims.claim: The same study found that after culturally proximate prompting the model texts remained less diverse than the human benchmark.
claims.source: Rong Zhao et al., arXiv 2604.20048v3, 8 June 2026
claims.quote: the model texts remained less diverse, more affectively positive

claims.claim: The three-model comparison in that study used GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4 and Gemini 2.5 Flash, producing 72,000 model-generated place texts.
claims.source: Rong Zhao et al., arXiv 2604.20048v3, 8 June 2026
claims.quote: The three-model comparison used GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4 and Gemini 2.5 Flash

claims.claim: A CSCW audit of LLM local knowledge found that in formal news contexts models exhibit an urban advantage, leaving rural areas systematically underrepresented with lower semantic depth.
claims.source: Zihan Gao and Jacob Thebault-Spieker, 'Is Your Chatbot a Tourist or a Townie?', Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction, 2026 (abstract as published by the UW-Madison Institute for Diversity Science, 24 April 2026)
claims.quote: leaving rural areas systematically underrepresented with lower semantic depth

claims.claim: The same audit found that models are more adept at concrete physical questions but consistently struggle to capture the nuanced relational and cognitive dimensions of a community.
claims.source: Zihan Gao and Jacob Thebault-Spieker, ACM CSCW 2026 (abstract via UW-Madison Institute for Diversity Science)
claims.quote: struggle to capture the nuanced relational and cognitive dimensions
